blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust in CPG & Brands meets two truths at once — volume keeps growing, and the old way stopped scaling. The structured response: the design question is what needs shared truth; the engineering answer is a governed ledger with the boring parts done properly.

Through the Blockchain & Digital Trust lens, the operating reality: CPG brands compete on shelf, on shelf-image and on data: trade spend efficiency, retail execution truth, demand signal quality and now provenance claims. The brands that win industrialize the sell-side data relationship with retailers.

Field execution blind is the concrete face of a general problem: the work is shaped for a world of manual checks and batch updates, while volume and scrutiny both grew. We start with the queue, the wait and the number they produce — not with a platform license.
In CPG & Brands, the recurring pressure points:

items: Retail-execution teams run route lists without shelf-truth priority; OOS persists.
Sustainability/origin claims face EUDR/DPP scrutiny; evidence manual.
Retailer portals and EDI produce a patchwork; trade-spend ROI is estimated.
Promotions, distribution changes and retail signals confuse planners; forecast error compounds.

blocks.x: In CPG & Brands, the pattern is provenance network — EUDR-grade chain-of-custody for claim SKUs. Claims verified sits on top as the measured result, tracked from the signed baseline onward. Around it, the design question is what needs shared truth; the engineering answer is a governed ledger with the boring parts done properly.

blocks.x: Delivery opens with measurement: the baseline for field execution blind is produced with your team and signed by whoever owns the number today. The working slice follows inside the quarter — Provenance network, bounded to one path, running on your estate. What we promise is modest and checkable: a signed baseline, a bounded slice in production, and evidence your auditors can read without a guide.

Two regimes anchor the Blockchain & Digital Trust frame in CPG & Brands: EUDR — commodity due diligence; DPP — product data duties approaching. Controls are designed in from the first sprint — not bolted on when the audit letter arrives.
